# Independent review of answered design sketches

2026-10-08. Reviewer: Codex, new independent advisor, neither proposal author nor coordinator. Design review only.

**EPIC-74 sketch — ADVISOR SIGNOFF: CHANGES REQUESTED.**

**EPIC-74 child acceptance amendment — CHANGES REQUESTED (inherits the parent blockers and adds the slice-boundary requirement below).**

**STORY-1486 sketch — ADVISOR SIGNOFF: CHANGES REQUESTED.**

The recorded directions stand: target/parent branches with canonical epic isolation; launch profile WITHOUT exemptions and with ordinary approval prompts preserved. These are not rejected directions. The exact proposals do not yet close the technical and authority gates required for architecture signoff. No implementation, dispatch, release of a hold, grant change, or merge is authorized by this report.

## Review identity and evidence

Read AGENTS.md, `.aida/discipline/two-seat-protocol.md`, `rework-brief-craft.md`, `seat-recovery-playbooks.md`, the complete ANSWERED_DESIGN_SKETCHES_READY.md, all three proposals, and the September target/parent plan. Read canonical JSON including descriptions, relationships, comments and operator answers for EPIC-74, STORY-1481/1482/1483/1486 and the authority dependency STORY-1473. Fresh snapshots are in `independent-sketch-review-evidence/` beside this report. Some earlier read calls reported cache contention; the final retained snapshots all report `cache.stale=false`. No cache rebuild or store sync was requested.

Local HEAD, main, origin/main and the read-only `git ls-remote origin refs/heads/main` observation agreed on **b46aec1e674baae5a329416d4119e67b59200a88**. All 19 files in the author's source-hash inventory matched both the supplied hashes and `git show main:<path>`; see `independent-sketch-review-evidence/source-integrity.json`. Additional source seams below were inspected in the clean tracked checkout at that main. This review concerns that exact main, not future external-agent changes.

| Reviewed artifact | Exact SHA-256 |
| --- | --- |
| EPIC74_AMENDED_SKETCH.md | `1105ae45cfa11db5a9c407e097ae5b95473bc4db8dbfa8ed1d515ac510e4f9a9` |
| EPIC74_CHILD_ACCEPTANCE_PROPOSED_AMENDMENT.md | `a50d69f0fcefa57f4e9953e8dcd9f31ae80fed90f6913f367e153a1a6b04d4c2` |
| STORY1486_AMENDED_SKETCH.md | `6bed750343f488083dc2fced9eb794e65f2c89dc8f32a5d205812358a7a81f75` |

EPIC-74 canonical comment `01a11c5a-e2df-7160-ac9d-012fd9331b18` and STORY-1486 comment `01a11c5b-255b-7b91-881d-243f9e2b5db5` exactly matched their proposal file bodies. The child artifact remains proposed text, not canonical acceptance.

Operator evidence: EPIC-74 `decision_request.answered=0`, answered at `2026-10-08T15:54:26.321418310Z`, selects “Target and parent branch model” and requires amended sketch/ADR while preserving store exclusion. STORY-1486 `answered=0`, answered at `2026-10-08T15:54:29.273727039Z`, selects “Profile without exemptions,” consequence “Scope writable roots and Git policy; preserve approval prompts.” Both selected resolutions are `noop`. Neither is a missing signoff or implicit answer to release authority/backend scope. Canonical parent/profile remain Draft; children remain Approved with their recorded guided/sketch gates. No canonical fields were changed here.

## Source findings

Line references below are to the pinned main and describe inspected source, not executed behavior.

| Source | Verified fact and review implication |
| --- | --- |
| `aida-core/src/pickability.rs:110`; `models.rs:1094` | Pickability currently reasons about human-only, triage and dependencies, not target isolation. Parent stores outgoing Parent edges to children; child stores reciprocal Child edges. A new resolver must handle missing/inconsistent reciprocal edges conservatively, not traverse the wrong direction or silently omit an ancestor. |
| `queue_cmd.rs:1250`, `8964`, `13094`, `13200` | Fresh pickup has a force-NeedsAttention shortcut. Plan resolution can synthesize/persist a queue row. Auto-complete has multiple projections, one dropping blocked reasons. Isolation cannot be implemented only as another optional reason at a caller that later discards it. |
| `burndown.rs:240`, `275`; `shift.rs:2648`; `backlog.rs:942`, `1195`; `integrate.rs:85`; `queue_cmd.rs:14478` | Separate candidate/classification paths exist. Shift turns queue-read failure into an empty vector and drops failed requirement lookups. Groom validates/enqueues separately. Integration classification does not carry isolation facts. The sketch's shared resolver is necessary but its current inventory is not proof of all call-site guards. |
| `mcp.rs:3528`, `4122`, `4982` | `claim_task` actually writes a lease; `queue_work` and `session_start` are metadata peeks returning CLI guidance. The proposed “MCP starts” wording must distinguish those. Guard the real claim mutation and make peeks display exclusion truthfully. |
| `pr_cmd.rs:1438`, `3334`, `4580` | The literal-main fallback is real. Ordinary PR creation uses the default branch; MR recovery accepts explicit/saved target. Neither provides canonical epic validation today. Recovery/resume and explicit target options are guard surfaces. |
| `lib.rs:60359`, `114519`; `merge_lock.rs:1`, `171`; `aida-core/src/db/git_backend.rs:1054`, `1137`, `1442`, `1525` | Wave/drain use branch merge leases. Canonical writes use a different store lock with atomic update facilities. A branch lease does not lock the graph. Wave constructs `match_head: None`; drain subsequently pins a reviewed head. “Use existing locks” without composition is insufficient. |
| `forge.rs:680`, `717`, `3051` | Existing merge options pin head; GitHub emits a head-match argument and GitLab sends `sha`. The inspected adapter contract has no corresponding expected-base/declaration revision field. Head pinning alone does not prevent a same-head PR retarget race. |
| `lib.rs:77289`, `77411`, `78267`, `75518` | Live/replay completion scan the local default branch; squash-body trailers can produce candidates. Reopen fences exist. Those fences applied only to a newly minted landing squash SHA cannot prove that old child work was refreshed after reopen. A coverage-aware gate must govern every promotion path. |
| `seat_authority.rs:104`, `146`, `211`, `235`; `lib.rs:53244` | Grant validation, roster ceiling, direct-human check and explicit child delegation exist; absent/invalid seat resolution falls back to implementer. Reuse these facts without describing that baseline as a guest grant or as an OS security boundary. |
| `session.rs:1288`, `1934`, `2431`, `2628` | Native Codex argv adds bypass only when selected; Codex headless argv always includes the bypass flag. Current bwrap builder binds the worktree writable and extra writable roots, provides writable tmp, and does not establish Git-operation/network mediation. Its preflight proves that a basic sandbox can run, not that this profile's guarantee holds. |
| `lib.rs:31561`; `aida_bin.rs:1`; `scaffold_cmd.rs` managed merge functions; `aida-core/src/scaffolding/settings.rs:24`, `mcp_translate.rs` | Dry planning, portable executable resolution and managed scaffold generation are existing reuse points. The executable resolver explicitly describes its ancestry check as an accident boundary, not a same-user security boundary. Hooks/settings generation does not prove whole-process confinement. |

## EPIC-74: required design rework

### E1 — Make selector closure and the first slice demonstrably safe

The proposal names the major families correctly, but must supply an entrypoint-to-guard matrix, including queue list/next/explicit pickup, forced pickup, auto-complete single/nextN/batch/cluster and resume/from-PR; burndown plan/run and wave merger; shift collection and dispatch; both groom forms; integration plan/run/watch; session/agent foreground/background/headless and resume; worktree entry; MCP peeks and claim_task; direct PR/ship, MR recovery, and completion reconciliation. Identify aliases by their shared handler rather than counting an alias as separate proof. Include already-open PRs and previously planned/queued work.

Every mutation must validate before its first queue/lease/status/worktree/launch/PR effect. Read surfaces may report a stale display, but cannot advertise an isolated spec as a valid pickup. Parse/read/ancestry failures must propagate as errors, especially through `shift::gather_candidates`, not disappear as empty success. Verify both in-scope positive selection and main-line exclusion with env unset, misleading env, explicit IDs and force/resume options.

**STORY-1481 amendment:** its independent release must already prevent isolated work reaching default through direct shipping, existing PRs, resume and reconciliation. Until STORY-1482 implements safe off-default PRs, unsupported off-default action paths must refuse. Merely filtering discovery while enabling a target-context launch that still ships to default does not satisfy slice 1. This is a staging dependency, not permission to merge all slices without review.

### E2 — Close the mutation-to-action race, not only the plan-to-check race

Concrete counterexample: read epic revision R, acquire target branch lease, validate R, release any store read guard, then another AIDA writer changes an ancestry edge/declaration before the forge call. The branch lease does not prevent that writer. A later evidence CAS can protect status, but cannot undo the wrong remote merge. The same issue exists before local pickup effects.

The revised ADR must name one lock/transaction ordering and linearization point shared by action admission and every isolation-affecting mutation. Either compose existing locks through the protected action or define a durable intent/reservation honored by those writers. Specify crash recovery, timeout/error handling and lock ordering; do not add a second independent lock convention without review. Validate an entire dependency set (graph and declaration generation, repository/default identity, relevant child evidence/reopen revision), not just the epic object's modification time. Avoid using a store HEAD equality that invalidates itself on its own evidence write; define expected inputs and outputs precisely.

Changing target to default, removing/reparenting a child, deleting/retyping an epic, restoring/importing records, or resolving a store conflict must not become alternate ways to clear isolation. A ref/default identity change must invalidate an action, not convert unfinished isolated work into ordinary eligible work. Keep an explicit isolation generation/evidence lifetime across clear/redeclare and remapped display IDs; use UUID identity.

For actual PR base/head: require immutable repository/forge identity and full source SHA, recheck under the correct target lease, and pin what the adapter can atomically pin. Document that current head pinning does NOT pin PR base. Serialize AIDA-mediated retargeting with merge; do not claim protection against concurrent raw forge retargeting unless a tested server-side precondition supplies it. Under the proposal's declared AIDA-mediated boundary, raw external mutations remain an explicit limitation; do not silently upgrade this to remote atomic consensus. If a required condition cannot be enforced by an adapter, refuse that protected action. Re-probe ambiguous network outcomes before retrying; a landed remote merge with failed local persistence retains isolation for idempotent reconciliation.

### E3 — Define squash coverage evidence and make replay obey it

“Snapshot coverage and independently validate it” is not yet an algorithm or schema. A child merge can be an ancestor of a landing head even after its changes were reverted. A squash removes ancestry to the landing result. Reusing a child trailer in a later squash produces a new commit SHA after a reopen without implementing the reopened acceptance. All three need explicit handling.

Require a versioned, durable coverage record containing repository identity, isolation generation, child UUID and evidence/reopen generation, actual child PR/base/head/merge commit, landing PR identity and exact reviewed head/base context, covered set, and verified actual landing result. Define where it lives in the existing model/history, how it is replicated, who may write it under existing authority, and how it survives clone/replay, ID remap and declaration clear. Old/malformed/unknown records must not imply coverage.

Separate mechanical inclusion from acceptance approval: establish child evidence ancestry to the reviewed source where applicable; require reviewed coverage of the final landing diff and explicitly exclude reverted/omitted child work. Pin the reviewed source and record the forge-confirmed squash result reachable from the authoritative default. A changed source, coverage set, child reopen or relevant base invalidates that review/manifest. Semantic equivalence cannot be inferred from commit titles, ancestry, patch-id alone or the current descendant set.

Preserve existing trailer grammar, but treat trailers as candidate attribution, not sufficient evidence for isolated lineage. Route live ship, auto-bump, replay, review-covers/umbrella promotion and retry through the same coverage validator. In particular, historical squash-body trailers must not bypass the exact covered set. Keep original child freshness checks even when final landing SHA is newer. Partial/intermediate-parent landing stays Done for uncovered work and never clears isolation; clear itself never completes a spec. These requirements apply after env is absent and after a declaration is later removed.

### E4 — Resolve technical choices; retain the unresolved authority fork

Decisions within the recorded direction:

- Epic-only typed declaration; no lane seat/flag/command family or per-spec override. Use canonical repo identity plus validated full branch ref. Reject ambiguous/conflicting/cyclic ancestry; unsupported nested distinct target declarations and multi-repository landing refuse.
- Represent parent internally as `Option<BranchRef>`. For default-target ordinary work, absent/empty parent normalizes to None and sync is a no-op with no Git merge invocation. Off-default with absent parent resolves to the positively identified repository default. An explicit same-as-target parent is a reported no-op. This follows Joe's quoted original empty-default wording without passing an empty string to Git. Persist/validate the effective parent in an operation plan; it is never an authority override.
- Generic `--force` cannot implicitly clear or bypass isolation. This is the required safe interim behavior under the selected isolation goal, not a newly invented permanent release entitlement. Existing unrelated force behavior stays outside this change.
- Verified complete final landing can use the existing authorized landing workflow to propose clear, only with covered-work checks and no concurrent/live/unlanded work escaping the inventory. Quiescence alone is not proof that unlanded work was deliberately released.

**Unresolved authority blocker:** canonical STORY-1481 still expressly promises force override and close-without-landing. The chosen branch vocabulary does not identify who may release live/unlanded isolation, whether that capability survives, or the evidence/confirmation required. Do not silently remove that product capability permanently, grant it to ordinary editors, or infer permission from “unattended proxy.” Record the bounded fork for coordinator disposition: an explicitly authorized audited release with complete live/unlanded inventory, or an explicit acceptance change forbidding such release. Until recorded authority resolves it, refuse affected release/target-reset/reparent mutations. No new operator prompt is sent by this review.

The ADR remains a required architecture artifact. The report resolves the mechanical parent choice; it does not supply the missing release authority or replace independent review of the revised race/coverage protocol.

### EPIC acceptance amendments and named tests

Retain the proposal's tests and add the following named obligations. All are future tests, not run or claimed passing here. Use temporary repositories, isolated HOME/AIDA roots, fake vendors/forges and process barriers; never live user/store state.

| Owner / acceptance | Required evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 1481 AC1–3, all selectors | `off_default_subtree_excluded_without_env_each_selector` expanded to the E1 matrix; `mcp_claim_isolation_refuses_before_lease`; `shift_isolation_read_failure_is_error`; `isolated_context_selects_only_subtree_positive`; `slice1_direct_ship_and_resume_fail_closed_before_slice2`. Assert zero effects and visible reasons, not just empty candidates. |
| 1481 AC3–5, revision/release | `ancestry_detach_target_reset_and_epic_delete_cannot_release`; `declaration_change_after_final_check_serializes_with_action`; `store_pull_generation_change_invalidates_plan`; `generic_force_does_not_release_isolation`; `clear_with_live_or_unlanded_work_refuses`. Use barriers after the final check, not only before it. An authorized positive release test waits for a recorded authority decision. |
| 1482 AC1, 1483 AC3 | `same_head_pr_retarget_during_merge_is_not_head_pinned`; `wave_drain_direct_and_mr_recovery_validate_target`; `trunk_default_missing_metadata_never_falls_back_to_main`; supported-path positive child merge and target-to-parent merge on both forges. Document raw-forge race boundary honestly. |
| 1482 AC2–4, 1483 AC3–4 | `squash_landing_completes_only_verified_covered_children`; `reverted_child_ancestor_is_not_coverage`; `reopened_child_old_work_in_new_squash_stays_open`; `squash_body_omitted_id_cannot_bypass_manifest`; `clone_replay_after_clear_retains_coverage_fence`; `landing_races_new_child_no_clear`; `remote_merge_success_local_persist_failure_reconciles_once`; intermediate-parent and closed-unmerged negatives. |
| 1483 AC1–2 | `default_target_empty_parent_sync_is_noop`; `off_default_parent_defaults_to_trunk`; `parent_sync_conflict_preserves_work_and_reports_drift`; unknown parent errors; shared branch is never automatically rebased/deleted. |

## STORY-1486: required design rework

### P1 — Strong Git read-only remains unmet, not narrowed

The sketch is candid and correctly rejects PATH wrappers, command filters, read-only `.git` alone and displayed workspace roots as sufficient enforcement. Current source validates that concern. Writable source/tmp permits repository creation and alternate Git state; readable network credentials and external tools can mutate remotely; writable shared Git metadata affects siblings. Current headless bypass and the current optional bwrap recipe cannot be certified as the selected restriction. No test was executed to probe the live host.

The profile needs a precise definition of protected operations/resources and a supported adapter design proving it. Under the retained strong wording, testing only `git commit` on the normal `.git` is inadequate. Define whether “Git write” includes new repositories and direct equivalent filesystem mutations; the proposal itself treats those as included, so it cannot keep an unrestricted writable scratch/source surface and claim universal prohibition. Ordinary editing and a prohibition on arbitrary Git-equivalent file writes require an explicit, coherent boundary. If a proposed backend must restrict that workflow or introduce a privileged/credential service, it needs its own authority/product scope, not an implementation inference here.

**Blocker:** no selected supported backend satisfies the strong contract while delivering the requested functional launch. Preserve AC2 and refuse unsupported restricted launches. A refusal-only implementation is not completion of the story. No permission is inferred to choose the weaker AIDA-mediated-only option. Narrowing the contract or authorizing a new enforcement architecture remains an explicit operator-owned fork; retaining the current stronger acceptance pending evidence is not a new product decision.

### P2 — Make the profile boundary complete and inspectable

The revised sketch/ADR must provide a vendor/OS/launch-mode capability matrix: foreground, background, headless, resume and inherited children; filesystem root precedence; git-dir/common-dir; symlinks, ancestor replacement and open writable handles; selected executable identity; child processes; network credentials; local sockets and out-of-process MCP/tool endpoints. A root list or successful basic bwrap self-test is not a capability certificate. Unconfined endpoints must be denied or covered by an independently validated boundary before calling the strong mode supported.

Restriction inheritance cannot rely on an environment string a child can remove, nor on re-resolving an invalidated guest grant as baseline implementer. Reuse seat authority but bind the launch restriction ceiling to the actual enforcement context. Report grant identity/source, requested mode, enforceable mode and refusal reason separately. No issuance/schema changes to the reserved authority work are authorized.

Close planning-to-spawn path replacement races with backend-supported handles/identities or refuse strong mode. Explain atomic application/rollback of scaffold updates and launch refusal before session/grant/lease/worktree effects. A preview can report unsupported; it must not launch a probe with uncontrolled side effects or create persistent authority state. Keep profile recipes symbolic; runtime-resolved paths may be printed, not persisted into portable generated artifacts. Shared common-dir scope and consumer/AIDA-checkout overlap need real confinement evidence, not path string assertions.

### P3 — Approval posture and acceptance amendments

Replace original AC3 exactly in substance: no generated exemption list, allow/no-ask entry, approval-policy-never setting or bypass flag; preserve the user's approval posture and refuse a restricted launch with an incompatible effective posture. Check the fully composed argv/config, including inherited user configuration and headless adapters, not just generated output. A prompted approval never overrides the profile ceiling. Do not change this running harness or global settings.

AC1 must test actual writable/read-only effects for consumer versus verified AIDA self-development identity, including parent/child mount overlap and shared administration. AC2 retains the strong guarantee and requires at least one genuinely supported positive restricted launch plus adversarial mutation negatives; unsupported-host refusal remains necessary but insufficient. AC4 reuses `aida_bin`, validates each selected binary at execution, and never interprets debug/release authorization as prompt exemption or permission for arbitrary `target/*`. AC5 covers every generated file, hook, command prefix and remediation snippet, with relocation tests. Add AC6 for pure preview, revalidation and monotonic child restrictions.

Named obligations: retain `consumer_profile_keeps_aida_checkout_read_only`, `aida_self_development_uses_verified_repo_identity`, `overlapping_roots_and_store_symlink_escape_refuse`, `git_read_only_cannot_be_widened_by_child_or_env`, `unsupported_git_boundary_refuses_before_spawn`, `generated_profile_preserves_approval_prompts`, `incompatible_existing_bypass_refuses_profile`, `debug_release_switch_needs_no_rescaffold`, `relocated_project_and_aida_install_keep_profile_portable`, `preview_then_grant_or_root_change_refuses_launch`, `preview_is_read_only`, and `shared_git_common_dir_is_explicit`.

Expand `supported_adapter_blocks_git_write_entrypoints` to absolute binaries, alternate index/object/git-dir, init/checkout/update-ref/commit, libgit2/direct equivalent writes, writable tmp, inherited FDs, child escalation attempts and unconfined MCP/socket endpoints. Add `readonly_remote_mutation_sends_no_request`, `grant_loss_does_not_widen_restriction`, `supported_profile_positive_read_edit_build_with_prompt`, and `approval_granted_does_not_lift_readonly`. Use a local fake forge/server and isolated credentials, recording before/after refs/files and requests. Positive editing/build tests must match the eventual supported workflow; do not silently delete functionality to obtain a negative-test pass. None of these tests has been run here.

## Exact proposed canonical comment bodies for coordinator relay

This assignment expressly prohibits spec changes. I therefore did not attempt canonical comment publication or probe/bypass a companion gate. These are proposed relay bodies, not posted canonical signoffs. No tool rejection is being claimed. Relay must retain independent authorship, exact proposal identity and all blockers; it must not turn CHANGES REQUESTED into approval or status/queue permission.

### EPIC-74 proposed comment

```text
ADVISOR SIGNOFF: CHANGES REQUESTED.

Independent reviewer: Codex, new strict advisor, not the sketch author or coordinator. Reviewed EPIC74_AMENDED_SKETCH.md SHA-256 1105ae45cfa11db5a9c407e097ae5b95473bc4db8dbfa8ed1d515ac510e4f9a9 and EPIC74_CHILD_ACCEPTANCE_PROPOSED_AMENDMENT.md SHA-256 a50d69f0fcefa57f4e9953e8dcd9f31ae80fed90f6913f367e153a1a6b04d4c2 against main b46aec1e674baae5a329416d4119e67b59200a88 and the canonical operator answer at 2026-10-08T15:54:26.321418310Z.

The target/parent direction is settled. Required rework: exhaustive entrypoint/guard matrix including MCP claim, direct ship, resume and MR recovery; safe slice-1 refusal until target shipping exists; a specified canonical graph/action lock or reservation protocol closing the AFTER-final-check race; honest head-versus-base pin limits; durable squash coverage and child-reopen generations enforced across live/replay/body-trailer promotion; and an ADR. Accept the technical parent representation Option<BranchRef>: None/no sync for ordinary default work, repository-default parent for off-default absent parent. No lane system or per-spec override.

Generic force cannot implicitly release isolation. The existing force/close-without-landing acceptance leaves a real authority fork: no recorded answer selects who may release live/unlanded work or its required evidence. Keep that fork explicit and refuse release-equivalent mutations until resolved; do not invent permanent capability removal or new editor/agent authority. Target reset, reparent/delete and default changes must not bypass isolation. Partial landing never clears; new squash SHA never refreshes old reopened child work by itself.

Full binding rework details, acceptance amendments, named tests, source references and publication limits: .aida/handoff/orchestrator/run-20261008/ANSWERED_DESIGN_SKETCHES_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md, sections E1–E4 and EPIC acceptance table. This is not implementation/dispatch/status/queue/merge authorization. TASK-1593 TASK-1591 BUG-1811 BUG-1812 remain external reservations. No tests were executed by this design review.
```

### STORY-1486 proposed comment

```text
ADVISOR SIGNOFF: CHANGES REQUESTED.

Independent reviewer: Codex, new strict advisor, not the sketch author or coordinator. Reviewed STORY1486_AMENDED_SKETCH.md SHA-256 6bed750343f488083dc2fced9eb794e65f2c89dc8f32a5d205812358a7a81f75 against main b46aec1e674baae5a329416d4119e67b59200a88 and the canonical operator answer at 2026-10-08T15:54:29.273727039Z.

Profile WITHOUT exemptions and preserved approval prompts is settled. Replace original exemption AC3 accordingly. The current native/headless/bwrap/root-list surfaces do not establish the strong Git-read-only contract. Require a supported backend and explicit operation/resource/threat boundary, actual-launch capability matrix, path/handle race closure, monotonic child restriction and out-of-process tool/network coverage. Preserve pure preview, portability, managed merge, existing seat validation and executable resolution. Inspect effective inherited config/argv, not just generated files.

Retain strong AC2. Unsupported restricted launch must refuse before session/grant/lease/worktree/spawn effects; refusal alone is not functional completion. No authority is inferred to narrow the guarantee to AIDA-mediated commands or to introduce a broker/new privileged enforcement architecture. That scope fork remains explicit until separately authorized. Approval never lifts the restriction. No exemptions, TTY bypass, new grants or global harness changes.

Full rework details, acceptance amendments, named positive/adversarial tests, source references and publication limits: .aida/handoff/orchestrator/run-20261008/ANSWERED_DESIGN_SKETCHES_INDEPENDENT_REVIEW.md, sections P1–P3. No implementation/dispatch/status/queue/merge authorization. TASK-1593 TASK-1591 BUG-1811 BUG-1812 remain external reservations. No tests were executed by this design review.
```

## Scope and final disposition

Only this report, read-only evidence snapshots/integrity record and the requested advisor mailbox notification are outputs of this review. No source, canonical comment/spec/status/queue, grant, reservation, hold, branch or deployment change was made. No test/build/launch was run; source counterexamples are static reasoning, not claimed reproduced exploits. Existing unrelated untracked files were preserved. No operator prompts were sent. The coordinator can relay the exact bodies within its own publication authority and route sketch rework; this review itself does not queue or launch it.

**Final verdict: CHANGES REQUESTED for both sketches and the companion child acceptance amendment.** Re-review revised exact hashes and ADR after the concrete technical rework; unresolved release authority and strong-profile enforcement/scope remain blockers, not implicit approvals.
